blocks.text: HOT TUB REMOVAL FAQ
Hot Tub Removal in Schomberg — What to Know Before You Book

items.q: How much does hot tub removal cost in Schomberg?
a: Pricing is confirmed on site once the crew sees the tub’s size, condition and how hard it is to get to — a portable spa costs less than a full six-seater with tight gate access. The number covers draining, cutting, hauling and disposal together, with per-unit pricing available if a builder needs several removals across a project.

items.q: Do you charge extra for rural properties or long laneways?
a: Yes — it’s regular work for us in Vaughan. Removal books against your project’s sequence like any other trade, with a committed date that holds, and per-project pricing for builders and renovation companies clearing more than one property.

items.q: Do I need to drain the hot tub myself before you arrive?
a: No — draining is part of the service. The Live Junk Free crew handles it safely on arrival, and you don’t need a hose, a pump, or any prep beyond making sure the area around the tub is reasonably accessible.

items.q: Is it safe to remove a hot tub that's still wired to electrical?
a: Only once the power is confirmed off. If your tub has a hardwired 240V connection, we ask that a licensed electrician disconnect it before the crew arrives — we don’t disconnect live electrical ourselves, for your safety and ours. Plug-in portable spas are simpler and usually just need unplugging.

items.q: Do you cover Lloydtown, Pottageville and Kettleby?
a: Completely, by design. Arrival times arrange around the family’s schedule, nothing is staged where the road can see it, and no client’s property is discussed with anyone outside the job.

items.q: Can you remove a hot tub the same day I call?
a: It shouldn’t, if it’s done right. Live Junk Free cuts the tub into sections small enough to clear the gate or deck opening rather than dragging or forcing the whole unit through, and protects deck boards, patio surfaces and landscaping along the removal path throughout.
